rows.Notes: Sourcing is these associates' bottleneck, so they generally accept. One associate who covers automotive is worth more than any number of passive profile views. Paste into LinkedIn People search: ("GLG" OR "AlphaSights" OR "Guidepoint" OR "Dialectica" OR "Third Bridge" OR "Coleman Research" OR "Atheneum" OR "proSapient" OR "NewtonX") AND ("Research Associate" OR "Client Service" OR "Client Protect" OR "Expert Sourcing" OR "Expert Recruiter" OR "Knowledge Broker"). Then run it again with each of these appended to surface sector coverage: "automotive", "mobility", "consumer", "industrials", "advertising", "media". Better still, filter by Current Company one network at a time and add the keyword, which beats one giant Boolean. Target 15 to 20 connections, US-based, associate or manager level. Connection note is Letter H in doc 05. Do NOT pitch in the note.

rows.Notes: REPLACES the Gravity step, which is out because the community is dormant. Two free tests instead, both stronger than the one they replace. First: post the thesis to your own LinkedIn feed. You have nearly 14,000 followers and 579 profile appearances a week, which is a real audience you already own, and posting the week the new headline goes live compounds both. Second: send Letter I to five agency owners you already know. Warmer than cold outreach, cheaper than a conference, and five replies tell you more about whether the framing lands than fifty impressions will. Run both before deciding Owner Camp.

rows.Notes: Source is the Nathan Thompson Voice & Tone Guide in Notion, under Frontier Life, Nathan's Personal, Personal Projects: . Sections 01, 02, 06, 08, and especially 10 are the load-bearing ones. The thing that would have saved today is the routing trigger: fire on anything written as Nathan (bio, post, email, note), and stand down explicitly for Sightbox and Vertical Vision client copy, where voice-for-venture governs. Getting that boundary right is the whole value.
